'''Christoph Carl Herbert''' "'''Chris'''" '''Adami''' (born August 30, 1962) is a German-American professor of microbiology and molecular genetics, as well as professor of physics and astronomy, at [[Michigan State University]]. He is a core faculty member of the Ecology, Evolution, and Behavior (EEB) Program there.<ref>{{cite web |title=EEB Core Faculty |url=https://eeb.msu.edu/people/core-faculty.aspx |website=EEB Program at MSU}}</ref>

==Education==
Adami was born in [[Brussels]], Belgium, and graduated from the [[European School of Brussels I]]. He obtained a [[Diplom]] in physics from the [[University of Bonn]] and an MA and a Ph.D. in theoretical [[nuclear physics]] from [[Stony Brook University]] in 1991.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.anderson.ucla.edu/x19853.xml|title=Chris Adami bio |website= anderson.ucla.edu|url-status= dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120207091936/http://www.anderson.ucla.edu/x19853.xml|archivedate=February 7, 2012}}</ref> Adami was a Division Prize Fellow in the lab of [[Steven E. Koonin]] at the [[California Institute of Technology]] from 1992-1995, and was subsequently on the Caltech faculty as a senior research associate.

==Career==
Before joining [[Michigan State University]], he was a professor of Applied Life Sciences at the [[Keck Graduate Institute]] in [[Claremont, California]]. Adami is best known for his work on [[Avida (software)|Avida]], an [[artificial life]] simulator used to study [[evolutionary biology]],<ref>{{cite journal|first=C.|last=Adami|year=2006|title=Digital Genetics: unravelling the genetic basis of evolution|journal=Nature Reviews Genetics|volume=7|pages=109–118|issue=2|doi=10.1038/nrg1771|pmid=16418746|s2cid=2677823}}</ref> and for applying the [[Information Theory|theory of information]] to physical and biological systems.  Together with [[Nicolas J. Cerf]], Adami made significant advances in the [[quantum information|quantum theory of information]] in the late 1990s.

==Honors==
He received the [[NASA Exceptional Achievement Medal]] while serving at [[JPL]], and was elected a [[AAAS Fellow|Fellow of the AAAS]] in 2012.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://news.msu.edu/story/10128/|title=MSU earns record number of AAAS Fellows|website=news.msu.edu|date=December 14, 2011}}</ref> He was also elected a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aps.org/newsroom/pressreleases/fellows17.cfm|title=American Physical Society Announces 2017 Fellows|website=www.aps.org|accessdate=October 3, 2021}}</ref> in 2017. On July 31, 2019, he was awarded the Lifetime Achievement Award by the International Society for Artificial Life.,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.alife.org/news/2019-isal-awards-winners|title=2019 ISAL Awards Winners|accessdate=October 3, 2021}}</ref> and the Beal Outstanding Faculty Award by Michigan State University in 2025.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://natsci.msu.edu/news/2025/2025-03-christoph-adami-beal-award.aspx|title=Christoph Adami honored with Beal Outstanding Faculty Award}}</ref>
